info.title: v1per admin API
info.description: Generated from the operation registry in crates/protocol. Commands need the request marker header and a same-origin Origin.

post.description:
Replaces the password after checking the current one, and ends every other session
 of the caller. A wrong current password is `invalid_credentials` and counts toward
 the login limit. The new password has 12 to 256 characters.

get.description: The caller's account. Reachable from an enrollment-only session.
The caller's own grants, by node name. Grants inherited from these are not listed.

post.description:
Creates a key and discloses its secret once. Needs reauthentication. Every
 capability must be key-grantable and held by the caller on the node, else
 `grant_exceeds_principal`. A node the caller cannot see is `not_found`. At most 50
 active keys per person.

get.description: The caller's keys, newest first, revoked ones included. Never the secret.

post.description:
Revokes one of the caller's keys at once. Requests with it answer like an unknown
 key. Revoking a revoked key answers the key unchanged.

Checks email and password. Wrong password and unknown email answer the same
 `invalid_credentials`. Without 2FA it sets the session cookie and answers
 `signed_in`. An enrolled account answers `second_factor_required` and sets a
 challenge cookie for `auth.verifySecondFactor`; the challenge is never a session. An
 account that must use 2FA but has not enrolled gets an enrollment-only session. 10
 attempts per client address per minute (`rate_limited`). A replayed key returns the
 stored answer without a new session or challenge.
Ends the current session and clears its cookie.

Checks the password, and the second factor when enrolled, and marks the current
 session for 10 minutes so sensitive commands pass. A wrong password is
 `invalid_credentials`, a missing second factor `second_factor_required`, a wrong one
 `second_factor_invalid`; none of them ends the session. Shares the login limit.

get.description: The signed-in account, or `null`. Answers signed-out callers too, never 401.

post.description:
Finishes a login with a time-based code or an unused recovery code and turns the
 challenge cookie into a session cookie. A wrong or used code is
 `second_factor_invalid`; after 5 wrong codes, or 5 minutes, the challenge ends and
 answers `unauthenticated`. Shares the login limit.

get.description:
The channels a monitor on `node` may use: those on the node and its ancestors,
 nearest node first, by name. Needs `node.read`. Channels on ancestors the caller
 cannot read are listed without their node. On the node's `channels:<id>` topic,
 which does not record changes on ancestors.

post.description:
Creates a channel on `node`. Needs `channels.manage`. With `apply_existing`, every
 monitor on the node and below uses it, like Kuma's "apply on all existing monitors".
Deletes a channel with its monitor links and delivery log. Needs `channels.manage`.

get.description:
A channel's deliveries, newest first. Needs `channels.manage` on its node. Pass
 `next_cursor` of a page as `cursor` for the next one.
One delivery, such as a test. Needs `channels.manage` on its node.

One channel with its settings. Needs `channels.manage` on its node. On the node's
 `channels:<id>` topic.

The channels on one node with their settings, by name. Needs `channels.manage`. On
 the `channels:<id>` topic.

The deliveries about one monitor, newest first, through the channels on its node
 and on the ancestors the caller can read. Needs `node.read` on the monitor's node.
 `error` and `detail` are left out for channels on nodes where the caller lacks
 `channels.manage`. Paged like `channels.deliveries`. On the monitor node's
 `channels:<id>` topic; a delivery through an ancestor's channel is announced on
 that node's topic.

post.description:
Queues a test message, Kuma's "Test" button, through the outbox with a single
 attempt. `settings` is the form as it stands; secret fields without `value` come
 from `channel`, which must be on `node`. Follow `channel.delivery` on the node's
 `channels:<id>` topic and read the outcome with `channels.delivery`. Needs
 `channels.manage`.

Replaces a channel's name, flags and settings. A secret field without `value` keeps
 its stored value. Needs `channels.manage` on the channel's node.
Creates a static component on `node`. Needs `pages.manage`.
Deletes a component; incidents stop naming it. Needs `pages.manage`.

get.description:
The components of a node, or with `subtree` of the node and every node below it, by
 name. Needs `node.read`. On the node's `components:<id>` topic.

post.description: Renames or describes a component. Needs `pages.manage` on its node.

get.description:
The Kuma import into `node`: its state, step progress and, once finished, the
 manifest. Instance admins only (`forbidden`); `not_found` when the node has none.

What the import into `node` did not map, or mapped with a loss, in source order.
 Instance admins only (`forbidden`); `not_found` when the node has no import.

Every Kuma import on the instance, newest first. Instance admins only
 (`forbidden`).

post.description:
Adds an update to the timeline. Targets it names that the incident did not affect
 yet are added. `resolved` ends the incident; another state reopens it, unless it is
 an auto-incident whose monitor has a newer open one (`invalid_value` on `state`).
 Marks an auto-incident as edited. Needs `incidents.manage`.

Opens an incident on `node` with its first update. Every target in `impacts` must
 be a monitor or static component on the node or below (`invalid_value` on
 `impacts`). Needs `incidents.manage`.

Deletes an incident with its timeline, such as an auto-incident dismissed as a false
 alarm. Needs `incidents.manage`.

get.description:
One incident with its affected targets and its timeline, oldest update first. Needs
 `node.read`. On the incident node's `incidents:<id>` topic.

The incidents of a node, or with `subtree` of the node and every node below it,
 newest first. Needs `node.read`. On the node's `incidents:<id>` topic.

schema.description: The incidents of every node below too.
Only incidents that affect this monitor.

get.description:
The pages the caller reads that show at least one of the incident's targets, and
 whether it is published there or due to be. Needs `node.read`. On the incident
 node's `incidents:<id>` topic.

post.description:
Publishes the incident to a page that shows at least one of its targets
 (`invalid_value` on `page` otherwise). Needs `incidents.manage` on the incident's
 node and on the page's.

Takes the incident off a page, and stops a pending auto-publication there. Needs
 `incidents.manage` on the incident's node and on the page's.

Changes the title and the affected targets. A target taken out loses its impact; one
 added has none until an update names it. Marks an auto-incident as edited. Needs
 `incidents.manage`.

get.description: Name, version and public URL of the instance.

Storage, probe, notification, retention and import health, as `v1per diagnostics`
 reports it. No event marks a change: read it again to refresh. Instance admins only
 (`forbidden`).
The instance settings. Instance admins only (`forbidden`).

post.description:
Queues a test email to `to` through `smtp` as given, or through the saved server
 without it (`required` on `smtp` when none is saved). A password without `value`
 uses the saved one. Follow `channel.delivery` on the root node's `channels:<id>`
 topic and read the outcome with `channels.delivery`. Five a minute per person
 (`rate_limited`). Instance admins only (`forbidden`).

Changes the instance settings. Instance admins only (`forbidden`). A setting the
 server configuration fixes (`name_fixed`, `public_url_fixed`) is ignored: its stored
 value stays as it is.

Sets or, without `smtp`, removes the instance SMTP server. Email channels without
 their own server send through it. A password without `value` keeps the stored one.
 Instance admins only (`forbidden`).

Redeems an invitation. A signed-in caller gets the grant; a signed-out caller passes
 `account` and gets a new account with the invited email and a session. Unknown,
 used, revoked and expired codes answer the same `not_found`. An email that already
 has an account is `invalid_value` on `account`: sign in first. A caller who already
 holds a grant on the node keeps it and the code stays unused.

get.description:
What an invitation code offers, for the join page. Unknown, used, revoked and
 expired codes answer `not_found`.

post.description:
Plans an active maintenance on `node`. `monitors` must be on the node or below
 (`invalid_value` on `monitors`). Needs `maintenance.manage`.
Deletes a maintenance. Needs `maintenance.manage`.

get.description: One maintenance with its next ten windows. Needs `node.read`.

The maintenances of a node, or with `subtree` of the node and every node below it,
 by title, each with its status and next three windows. Needs `node.read`. On the
 node's `maintenance:<id>` topic.

post.description: Stops a maintenance: no window applies until it resumes. Ends a `manual` one.

get.description:
The next ten windows of a schedule that is not saved yet, for the editor. Invalid
 fields answer `invalid_arguments`. On the `instance` topic.

schema.description: `HH:MM`. An end before the start runs past midnight.
The last day of every month too.
Five fields, or six with seconds first.
An IANA zone such as `Europe/Vienna`; absent means the instance timezone.

post.description: Lets a paused maintenance's windows apply again. Starts a `manual` one.
Replaces a maintenance's title, schedule and monitors. Needs `maintenance.manage`.

get.description:
Invitations to the node, newest first. Needs `members.manage`. On the `members:<id>`
 topic.

post.description:
Creates a single-use invitation for one role on the node and discloses its link
 once. Needs `members.manage`, and the role must pass the rank rule. Lifetime 1 to 30
 days, 7 by default.

get.description:
Everyone who can access the node: grants on it and its ancestors, and instance
 admins. Needs `node.read`. On the `members:<id>` topic, which also hears of grant
 changes on ancestors and of moves that change the ancestors.

post.description:
Removes someone's grant on the node. Anyone may remove their own; removing another
 person's needs `members.manage` and the rank rule. Grants on ancestors stay.
Revokes a pending invitation. Needs `members.manage` on its node.

Changes someone's grant on the node. Needs `members.manage`; the caller must outrank
 the person's effective role and the new role (R-RANK). Raising to admin or owner
 needs reauthentication.

Creates an active monitor on `node`. Needs `monitors.manage`. Secret fields need a
 `value`. A push monitor without `push_token` gets a random 32-character token.
 `group` must be a group monitor on the node or an ancestor the caller can read.
 `probes` must be probes `probes.available` offers on the node, else `invalid_value`
 on `probes`; the same holds for `channels` and `channels.available`. Without
 `channels` it uses the default channels on the node and its ancestors.

get.description:
Daily bars for the last `days` days in `timezone`, today included: of the monitor,
 or of one `probe`'s own results.

schema.description: One probe's own results instead of the monitor's status.
An IANA zone such as `Europe/Vienna`; default `UTC`.

post.description:
Deletes a monitor with its state. Members of a deleted group leave the group.
 Recorded heartbeats stay until retention removes them. Needs `monitors.manage`.

get.description:
One monitor with its settings, current state and the state on each probe. Secrets
 show only whether they are set; the push token only to callers with
 `monitors.manage`. On the `monitors:<id>` topic.

Recorded heartbeats, newest first, from every probe or from `probe` only. Pass
 `next_cursor` of a page as `cursor` for the next one.

Latency of up beats per bucket in `[from, to)`, at most 1,500 buckets: of the
 monitor, or of one `probe`'s own results.

schema.description: One probe's own results instead of the monitor's status.

get.description:
The monitors on one node, or with `subtree` on the node and every node below it,
 with their current status, last latency and 24-hour uptime, by name. Needs
 `node.read`. On the `monitors:<id>` topic, with `subtree` on `monitor-tree:<id>`.

schema.description: The monitors of every node below too.

post.description: Stops checking a monitor. Its status stays as it was. Needs `monitors.manage`.

Starts checking a paused monitor again, at once. A monitor of an unsupported type
 cannot resume (`invalid_value` on `monitor`). Needs `monitors.manage`.

Sets or clears the status of a manual monitor, recorded at once and then every
 interval. Other types answer `invalid_value` on `monitor`. Needs `monitors.manage`.

Replaces a monitor's settings. Needs `monitors.manage`. A secret field without
 `value` keeps its stored value. The type may change; status history stays. Without
 `channels` its channels stay as they are.

get.description:
Uptime over 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days and 1 year, counted like Uptime Kuma: of the
 monitor, or of one `probe`'s own results.

schema.description: One probe's own results instead of the monitor's status.

post.description:
Creates a node as the last child of `parent`. Needs `node.write` on the parent. A
 node sits at most 8 levels below the root (`too_many` on `parent`).

Deletes a node. Needs `node.delete` and reauthentication. A node with descendants
 needs `descendants` set to their number, else `node_not_empty` with that number in
 `current`; then the whole subtree with its grants, invitations and API keys goes.
 The root cannot be deleted.

get.description: One node with its path. Needs `node.read`. On the `node:<id>` topic.

post.description:
Moves a node with its subtree to the end of another parent. Needs `node.move` on the
 node and `node.write` on the current and the new parent. The root cannot move, a node
 cannot move below itself (`invalid_value` on `parent`) and the subtree must stay
 within 8 levels (`too_many` on `parent`). Who sees the subtree changes with it.
Renames a node. Needs `node.write`.

Moves a node to `position` among its siblings, counted from 0; past the end means
 last. Needs `node.write` on the parent.

Requires 2FA of everyone holding a grant on the node or below it, or lifts that
 requirement. Needs `members.manage` and reauthentication. Sessions without a second
 factor become enrollment-only at their next request.

get.description:
The tree as the caller sees it, depth first with siblings in order: every node the
 caller can read, and the ancestors above them as placeholders without a name. On the
 caller's `user:<id>` topic, which records every change to what they see.

post.description:
Routes requests whose `Host` is `hostname` to the page. The hostname must be
 unclaimed and not this instance's own (`invalid_value` on `hostname`). Needs
 `pages.manage`.

Creates a page on `node`, restricted to grant holders until `pages.updateAccess`
 opens it. The slug must be unused (`invalid_value` on `slug`). Needs `pages.manage`.

Creates a share token. Its secret is answered once: open the page at
 `/s/<slug>/t/<secret>` or with `?token=<secret>`. Needs `pages.manage`.

Deletes a page with its layout, hostnames, share tokens and publications. Needs
 `pages.manage`.

get.description:
One page with its settings, access, layout and share tokens. Needs `node.read`. On
 the page node's `pages:<id>` topic.

The pages of a node, or with `subtree` of the node and every node below it, by
 title. Needs `node.read`. On the node's `pages:<id>` topic.

The snapshot `audience` would get, in `locale` or the page's default. Needs
 `node.read`. On the page's `page:<id>` topic.

post.description: Stops routing `hostname` to the page. Needs `pages.manage`.
Removes the logo. Upload one with `POST /api/pages/<id>/logo`. Needs `pages.manage`.

Revokes and deletes a share token; pages opened with it close at the next check.
 Needs `pages.manage`.
Replaces the page's settings. Needs `pages.manage`.

Replaces public access, the password, and the addresses and domains that may
 request sign-in links. A new or cleared password signs out everyone who entered
 the old one. Needs `pages.manage`.

Replaces the groups and their components in one step. A component keeps its ID
 while its target stays on the page, and a group while its `id` is sent. Targets
 must be monitors or static components on the page's node or below, each once
 (`invalid_value` on `groups`). Needs `pages.manage` and the page's current
 `revision`.

get.description:
The probes a monitor on `node` may use: those registered on the node and its
 ancestors, not revoked, nearest node first, with their node where the caller reads
 it. Needs `node.read`. On the node's
 `probes:<id>` topic, which does not record changes on ancestors.

post.description:
Registers a remote probe on `node` and discloses its token once. Needs
 `probes.manage`. Run the agent with `v1per probe --server <url> --token <secret>`.

get.description:
The probes registered on one node with their health, oldest first, revoked ones
 included. Needs `node.read`. On the `probes:<id>` topic.

post.description:
Revokes a probe's token at once: the agent's next request is refused and the probe
 leaves every monitor it served. Needs `probes.manage` on the probe's node. The
 built-in probe cannot be revoked (`invalid_value` on `probe`). Revoking a revoked
 probe answers it unchanged.

Starts enrollment, or reenrollment while enrolled: creates a pending secret and
 discloses it once. The active factor, if any, keeps working until `twoFactor.confirm`.
 Calling it again replaces the pending secret. Reachable from an enrollment-only
 session. Reenrollment needs reauthentication; a first enrollment does not.

Confirms the pending secret with a current code, makes it the active factor and
 discloses a fresh set of 10 recovery codes once. An enrollment-only session becomes a
 full session. A wrong code is `second_factor_invalid`; no pending secret is
 `invalid_arguments` on `code`. Replacing a confirmed factor needs reauthentication.

Removes the factor and its recovery codes. Needs reauthentication. When a node
 requires 2FA of the caller, their sessions become enrollment-only at the next request.
Replaces every recovery code with 10 new ones, disclosed once. Needs reauthentication.

message.description: English text for logs and developers. Not shown to people and not stable.

errors.description: Field errors keyed by argument name, for `invalid_arguments`.

current.description: The current revision for `stale_revision`, the descendant count for `node_not_empty`.

ApiErrorBody.description: The body of every non-2xx API answer.

oneOf.description: No valid credential. Sent whether or not the resource exists.
Wrong password or unknown account. Both answer identically.
The password was correct; a second factor is needed next.
A wrong, used or unreadable time-based or recovery code.

The session may only enroll a second factor: a node the person holds a grant on, or an
ancestor of it, requires 2FA.
A sensitive command needs a password check within the last 10 minutes.
Missing, hidden and unknown resources and operations all answer with this code and the same body.
The resource is visible but the role lacks the capability.
API keys cannot call this operation.
An API key would hold a capability its owner lacks on the node, or one only people hold.
A mutation without the request marker or from another origin.
`expected_revision` is older than the resource. `current` carries the head.
The idempotency key was used for another operation or other arguments.

The node has descendants and the request did not confirm their number. `current`
carries the number of descendant nodes.
The request does not parse: bad JSON, wrong types, missing idempotency key.
Arguments parse but fail validation. `errors` names each field.
The body or query string exceeds its byte limit.
A query ran past its 30 second budget and was cancelled.

limit.description: The limit that was exceeded, for `too_short`, `too_long` and `too_many`.

oneOf.description: More items than the limit allows.

idempotency_key.description:
Repeating a key repeats the same intent: the stored answer comes back without running
the command again. 1 to 128 characters, kept for 24 hours.

revision.description:
Sequence of the last topic event the command recorded, or the `instance` head when it
recorded none.

Head of the snapshot's topic, read in the same transaction as the data. Pass it as
`expected_revision` to a command that changes the same resource.

cursor.description: `<topic>@<revision>`. Opaque to the browser; subscribe from it to follow the snapshot.

api_base.description: Path prefix of the admin API, without a trailing slash.

version.description: Server version, shown in the sidebar footer.

instance_name.description: The operator's name for this instance, shown in the shell and the document title.

RuntimeConfig.description: Served uncached, so a changed server setting reaches the browser without rebuilding the app.

Empty.description: Arguments of operations that take none.

instance_admin.description:
Manages instance settings, SMTP, shared probes, backups and the root node, and acts as
owner of the root.

NodeId.description:
A node of the tree. A SQLite row ID that is never reused, like monitor and probe IDs, and
sent as a decimal string like every other ID.

oneOf.description: See the node, its subtree, members, monitors, status pages and incidents.
Rename the node, create and order its children.
Invite, change and remove grants under the rank rule, and require 2FA.
Move the node to another parent.
Delete the node and, with confirmation, its subtree.

Capability.description: What a node scope allows. A closed set: every node-scoped operation names one.

secret.description: The full secret for `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. `null` in a replayed answer.

secret_withheld.description: True when this answer is a replay and the secret was withheld.

prefix.description: The first characters of the secret, to tell keys apart.

node.description: The key reaches this node and its subtree.

oneOf.description: A full session cookie is set.
A challenge cookie is set; call `auth.verifySecondFactor` next.

An enrollment-only session cookie is set: only `twoFactor.begin`, `twoFactor.confirm`,
`account.get` and `auth.logout` answer until enrollment is confirmed.

LoginResult.description: The outcome of a correct password or second factor.

second_factor.description: Needed when the account is enrolled in 2FA.

oneOf.description: The current 6-digit code of the authenticator app.
One unused recovery code. Spaces and dashes are ignored, letters are not case sensitive.

reauthenticated_until.description: Sensitive commands pass until this instant.

enrollment_only.description: The session may only enroll a second factor. False when signed out.

reauthenticated_until.description:
Sensitive commands pass without a password prompt until this instant. Absent when the
session has not reauthenticated or the window has passed.

provider.description: Kuma's provider type, such as `smtp` or `discord`.

own.description: On the node itself rather than on an ancestor.

ChannelChoice.description: A channel a monitor may use.

ChannelId.description: A notification channel, owned by one node and usable in its subtree.

is_default.description: New monitors on the node and below use it unless their creator picks channels.

active.description: An inactive channel queues nothing. Default on.

apply_existing.description: Links every monitor on the node and below to the channel.

oneOf.description:
An imported Kuma provider v1per does not send to yet. Its settings stay sealed. Never
accepted by `channels.create` or `update`.

ChannelSettings.description:
A provider's settings, with Kuma's field meanings under snake_case names. Tagged by Kuma's
`type`.

clear.description: Removes the stored value. Requests only; not together with `value`.

set.description: A value is stored. Ignored in requests.

SecretField.description:
A sealed credential. Send `value` to set or replace it, `clear: true` to remove it so the
check sends an empty value, or neither to keep the stored one. Answers never carry the
value, only whether one is set.

secure.description: Implicit TLS. Off means STARTTLS when the server offers it.

ignore_starttls.description: Only with `secure` off: never upgrade to TLS.

to.description: Comma-separated addresses. At least one of `to`, `cc` and `bcc` is needed.

custom_subject.description: A Liquid template with Kuma's variables.

custom_body.description: A Liquid template with Kuma's variables.

additional_headers.description: A JSON object of extra headers.

dkim_skip_fields.description: Colon-separated header names to leave unsigned.

SmtpChannel.description:
Email. Without `host` the instance SMTP server sends it, and an absent `from` uses the
instance sender.

use_message_template.description: Kuma's older switch for a custom template, read only without `message_format`.

message_template.description: A Liquid template with Kuma's variables.

custom_body.description: The body for `content_type: custom`, a Liquid template with Kuma's variables.

additional_headers.description: A JSON object of extra headers, often with a token.

include_group_name.description: Absent counts as on, as in Kuma.

inactive_reason.description: Why an imported channel cannot send, such as an unsupported provider.

revision.description: Rises with every change. Pass it as `expected_revision` to `channels.update`.

Channel.description: A channel as stored. Secrets show only whether they are set.

next_cursor.description: `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last one.

channel.description: Absent for a test of an unsaved form.

summary.description: Kuma's message line, such as `[API] [🔴 Down] timeout`.

next_attempt_at.description: When a pending delivery is tried next.

detail.description: What the provider answered to the successful attempt.

Delivery.description: One message for one channel. Never holds a secret.

DeliveryId.description: One message for one channel in the notification outbox.

MonitorId.description: A monitor, owned by one node.

oneOf.description: Waiting for its first attempt or a retry.
The provider refused it for good, or retries ran out after 24 hours.
Not sent: its monitor is under maintenance.

channel.description: The saved channel the form edits, for its stored secrets.

name.description: Used in the test message, `<name> Testing`.

expected_revision.description:
The channel's `revision` the edit is based on; `stale_revision` with the current one
otherwise.

is_default.description: New monitors on the node and below use it unless their creator picks channels.

active.description: An inactive channel queues nothing. Default on.

apply_existing.description: Links every monitor on the channel's node and below to it.

ComponentId.description: A static component: a part of a service without a monitor, owned by one node.

source.description: The Kuma database as named on the command line.

manifest.description: Present once the import is complete.

oneOf.description: In progress, or interrupted: `v1per import kuma` with the same source resumes it.

skipped.description: Source rows left out, such as history of a deleted monitor.

oneOf.description:
Nodes, monitors, channels, maintenance, pages, incidents, users and the inventory, in
one transaction.
Kuma's `stat_*` rollups.
Raw heartbeats inside the retention window.
Counts and uptime compared with the source; writes the manifest.

ImportStep.description: Steps in the order they run.

reconciled.description: Every table, history count and uptime window matches.

raw_since.description: Raw heartbeats at or after this instant were imported.

logins.description: Kuma users with the login they sign in with now.

notes.description: Losses that have no inventory row, such as tag colors.

ImportManifest.description: What an import created, compared with its source. Written to the data directory as well.

sha256.description: Of the database file followed by its WAL, when one was read.

unchanged.description: The source hashed the same before and after the import.

inventoried.description: Inventory entries for the table. A paused monitor is mapped and inventoried.

destination.description: v1per rows of the counterpart, where there is one table to count.

TableCheck.description: One Kuma configuration or inventory table.

skipped.description: Rows of monitors that no longer exist in the source.

outside_window.description: Heartbeats before the raw retention window; only their rollups are imported.

HistoryCheck.description: One history table: `heartbeat` or a `stat_*` table.

as_of.description: The windows end with the bucket holding this instant: the newest one Kuma wrote.

matched.description: Monitors whose 24 hour, 30 day and 1 year counts equal Kuma's.

WindowCheck.description: Up and down beats in one window, pending counted as down and maintenance left out.

uptime.description: From 0 to 1; absent without up or down beats.

oneOf.description: Kuma's bcrypt hash, replaced with argon2 at the first sign-in.
Inactive in Kuma or a legacy hash: an instance admin sets a new password.

next_cursor.description: `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last one.

label.description: A name to recognise it by, never a secret.

columns.description: Source columns kept with it; their values are sealed.

source.description: The Kuma database as named on the command line.

reconciled.description: The manifest's verdict, once the import is complete.

ImportSummary.description: One import, without its steps and manifest; `imports.get` has those.

impacts.description: Targets whose impact changes, each once.

IncidentId.description: An incident, owned by one node.

Target.description: A monitor or a static component an incident names.

Impact.description: How badly a component is affected, from best to worst.

impact.description: The worst impact among the affected targets; absent while none has one.

auto_monitor.description: The monitor whose down transition opened it, while that monitor exists.
